Portfolio protection

What does the hedge cost?

1 MWh each hour in each zone. All scenarios enforce a shared €60 daily premium budget and 8 MWh open-volume limit.

UnhedgedWith paper caps

Cost = spot price × load + premium paid − cap payout. Payout = hedged MWh × max(hourly price − strike, 0). Premiums are attributed to delivery days for cost comparison; risk checks charge them on issue days.

Trade management / default €8, 50% scenario

Method, audit trail and limitations
  • Source: Energinet Day-Ahead Prices. Four 15-minute EUR/MWh observations are averaged into one hourly reference price. No missing-value interpolation.
  • Training: first eligible observation through 30 April 2026. Validation: 4 May–28 June. Simulated model lock: 30 June. Test: 2 July–29 September. No refit on validation or test.
  • Decision = delivery minus 48 hours. Newest price feature starts 24 hours before decision. Calendar features refer to delivery time in UTC. Archived revisions are not point-in-time publication records.
  • One L2-regularized logistic model per zone, compared with the training spike frequency and a trailing-week frequency. The 90th-percentile strike, scaling and coefficients use training only. Candidate selection uses validation Brier only.
  • 20% alert trigger is illustrative, not an optimal option-pricing rule. It ignores expected spike severity. Contract premiums do not vary with market risk.
  • No exchange connection, real fills, collateral, taxes, transaction costs or counterparty risk. Open-volume and daily-budget limits are portfolio-wide. Kill-switch behavior is implemented and tested in the ledger.
  • Hourly-average caps may have different payoffs from quarter-hour products. Risk summaries use 90 complete UTC days, and only five days in the worst-5% mean; these are historical cost statistics, not forward loss guarantees.
  • Probabilities may deteriorate under a new price regime. Ranking skill is insufficient evidence of reliable probabilities or an executable hedge.
